appraisal_events.evidence: Aimé... tint à me dire que Dreyfus était mille fois coupable. « On saura tout... c'est un monsieur très lié dans l'état-major qui me l'a dit. »
appraisal_events.explanation: Aimé pronounces Dreyfus guilty and relays secondhand certainty from a supposedly well-connected informant, staged with comic self-importance through his mimicry of the source's gesture, which frames the claim as unreliable gossip rather than narrator-endorsed fact.

status_effects.explanation: Dreyfus is declared guilty by a minor character relaying fashionable rumor, though the passage's comic, performative framing of the source undercuts the authority of the claim.

ambiguities: Aimé's claim about Dreyfus's guilt is presented through a comic, secondhand chain of gossip (an unnamed 'monsieur très lié dans l'état-major'), so the narrator's own endorsement of the judgment is unclear.
